title: Targeted winter kindness meets older residents at the intersection of energy hardship, food trade-offs, loneliness and information access
source_unit: Ipsos for Small Acts of Kindness, Warm in Winter and Bags of Kindness recipient feedback, September 2026 release
geography: Hertfordshire and Bedfordshire, England; nominated older and vulnerable residents receiving charity gift bags

observations.period: October–December 2025; recipient feedback on cost and energy pressure

denominator.unit: opt-in recipients who returned complete or partially completed questionnaires after receiving a Warm in Winter or Bag of Kindness gift

cost_of_living_negative.unit: percent saying the rising cost of living negatively affected them; 12% described the impact as large

energy_cost_negative.unit: percent saying rising energy costs negatively affected them; 24% described the impact as large

heating_affected.unit: percent saying cost-of-living increases affected their heating

food_purchase_affected.unit: percent saying cost-of-living increases affected the food they buy

household_tradeoff.value: energy and food choices are reported as linked consequences of cost pressure among recipients

observations.method: Paper questionnaires placed in charity gift bags and returned by recipients through prepaid post; participants were nominated by community members and were not sampled from the general population.
observations.uncertainty: The opt-in recipient sample is selected for vulnerability and receipt of support; results do not estimate prevalence among older people, identify a counterfactual, or establish that the gift bags caused any change.
observations.subgroup: Older and vulnerable residents in Hertfordshire and Bedfordshire who received one of the charity bags and chose to return a questionnaire.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reported cost pressure may predate the intervention, be concentrated among people nominated for support, or reflect seasonal recall rather than a general winter trend.

denominator.unit: opt-in recipients who returned complete or partially completed questionnaires after receiving a charity gift bag

isolation_any.unit: percent reporting feelings of isolation at least some of the time

isolation_some_time.unit: percent feeling isolated some of the time

isolation_most_or_all.unit: percent feeling isolated most or all of the time

television_radio_company.unit: percent agreeing that television or radio is their main source of company

social_connection_route.value: loneliness, energy insecurity and media-mediated companionship appear together in the support-recipient experience

observations.method: Self-completed paper feedback questionnaire with an open support-recipient frame; percentages are source-reported and item completion may vary.
observations.uncertainty: The survey does not measure network size, contact frequency, mental-health diagnosis, media use duration, or whether the gift changed isolation or companionship.
observations.subgroup: Opt-in charity-bag recipients in Hertfordshire and Bedfordshire.
observations.counterinterpretation: Television or radio may provide routine and comfort without indicating absence of other relationships; isolation reports may also be influenced by nomination and receipt context.

observations.period: October–December 2025; material aid, printed information and perceived care

denominator.unit: opt-in recipients who returned complete or partially completed questionnaires after receiving a charity gift bag

everything_almost_everything_useful.unit: percent spontaneously saying everything or almost everything in the bag was useful

warm_clothing_useful.unit: percent highlighting warm clothing as useful

printed_information_useful.unit: percent finding the Purple Pages information pack useful

printed_information_important.unit: percent saying it is important for organisations and charities to produce printed information

felt_good_or_cheered.unit: percent whose open-ended response described feeling good, happy, delighted or cheered up

felt_cared_for.unit: percent whose open-ended response expressed feeling loved, thought of or cared for

observations.method: Ipsos coding of recipient feedback, including open-ended responses, combined with structured usefulness and information questions.
observations.uncertainty: Usefulness, emotion and information preferences are recipient reports; the survey does not measure warmth, bill reduction, service take-up, health, or sustained connection after the gift.
observations.subgroup: Opt-in charity-bag recipients in Hertfordshire and Bedfordshire.
observations.counterinterpretation: Positive responses may reflect gratitude, novelty, social desirability or relief at recognition and should not be interpreted as evidence that small material gifts substitute for structural support.

observations.period: Winter 2024–25 compared with winter 2023–24; repeated recipient feedback route

denominator.unit: prior-wave recipients under the same charity-feedback methodology

information_pack_useful_prior_wave.unit: percent finding the Purple Pages information pack useful in the prior wave

comparison_scope.value: the source compares 618 current-wave responses with 546 prior-wave responses using the same broad method

intervention_learning.value: the charity can use repeated recipient feedback to tune material and information support, but the design does not identify counterfactual effect or population change

observations.method: Repeated cross-sectional feedback among recipients of the charity's bags, with questionnaires returned voluntarily in both waves.
observations.uncertainty: The waves are not a matched panel, recipients may differ, item completion is optional, and repeated usefulness does not establish improved outcomes over time.
observations.subgroup: Charity-bag recipients in the two local counties across the 2024 and 2025 winter waves.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable usefulness ratings could indicate consistent design quality, stable unmet need, or recurring gratitude rather than intervention effectiveness.

related_sources.claim: Ipsos primary release with recipient sample, cost, energy, heating, food, loneliness, usefulness, information and emotional-response results.
Charity context for Warm in Winter, Bags of Kindness and the local support model.

boundary: This record adds an intervention-encounter route: targeted material warmth, printed information and recognition meet energy hardship, food trade-offs, isolation and mediated companionship among nominated older and vulnerable residents. It is an opt-in recipient feedback sample from Hertfordshire and Bedfordshire, not population prevalence, a randomized evaluation, a matched panel, or evidence that the bags caused changes in bills, food security, health, loneliness or service take-up.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Ipsos primary release reviewed for recipient frame, field/wave timing, sample sizes, cost and energy impacts, heating and food trade-offs, isolation, media companionship, usefulness, printed information, emotional coding and prior-wave comparison.
